questions.q: Give an account of the major international conventions dealing with the environment.
answer: Several international conventions have been signed to protect different aspects of the environment.

answer.text: The Convention on Biological Diversity, adopted at the Rio Earth Summit of 1992, aims to conserve biodiversity, use it sustainably and share its benefits fairly, through the Cartagena and Nagoya protocols. CITES of 1973 regulates international trade in endangered species, while the Ramsar Convention of 1971 protects wetlands.

The Basel Convention controls the movement of hazardous wastes across borders, the Rotterdam Convention governs trade in hazardous chemicals, and the Stockholm Convention of 2001 targets persistent organic pollutants.
The Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol protect the ozone layer, while the UNFCCC, the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement address climate change.

answer: Together these treaties form a global framework for protecting the environment.
